$$F(\rho):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho H_N^\sigma)-k_BT\,s(\rho),$$

nonzero finite-dimensional sector), the number $F_{\mathrm{eq}}:=-\beta^{-1}\log Z_N$
is called the **equilibrium free energy**; it is the value of the functional
at $\rho_\beta$ by the cited theorem.

**(b) The Lueders instrument of a declared ideal sharp measurement.** For a preparation $\rho$ the **outcome probabilities** are
$$p_{a}:=\operatorname{tr}(\rho P_{a})\ge0,\qquad \sum_{a}p_{a}=1,$$
and for a pure preparation of the unit ray $[\psi]$ they are $p_{a}=\|P_{a}\psi\|^{2}$ (clause (ii) of P3, read with the outcome law of [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). If $p_{a}>0$ the **conditional state** after the outcome $a$ is the selective Lueders update
$$\rho_{a}:=\frac{P_{a}\rho P_{a}}{p_{a}};$$
it is a state with $\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{a}P_{a})=1$ and $P_{a}\rho_{a}P_{a}=\rho_{a}$ ([[lem-nrqm-measurement-selective-luders-update]], clause (iii) of P3). If the outcomes are recorded but not selected, the **discarded-outcome state** is
$$\Phi(\rho):=\sum_{a\in A}P_{a}\rho P_{a},$$
the trace-norm convergent series of [[lem-nrqm-measurement-nonselective-luders-map]]; it is a state with $\Phi(\rho)=\sum_{a:p_{a}>0}p_{a}\rho_{a}$ and $\operatorname{tr}(\Phi(\rho)P_{a})=p_{a}$ (clause (iv) of P3).

**(f) Limits.** Declared ideal sharp measurements are idealizations of apparatus that are idealized as repeatable and projection-valued; the framework does not assert that every apparatus, or any particular apparatus, is of this form (clause (v) of P3). **(c) Assigned energy observables.** Let $\mathcal F_{2}$ be the unitary
Plancherel transform of
[[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clause (b), $c:=2\pi^{2}\hbar^{2}/m$, and let
$$H^{\mathrm{free}}:=\mathcal F_{2}^{*}M_{c|\xi|^{2}}\mathcal F_{2},\qquad D(H^{\mathrm{free}}):=\bigl\{f\in H_{0}:|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f\in H_{0}\bigr\}$$
be the free operator of that clause with $d=3$ and $b=0$; by
[[lem-nrqm-central-free-operator-differential-identification]] its domain is
the Sobolev space $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R^{3};\mathbb C)$
([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]) and
$H^{\mathrm{free}}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\Delta_{w}f$ with $\Delta_{w}$ the
weak Laplacian ([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]).
For equations in physical coordinates write $A_{0,x}:=-\Delta_x^{\mathrm{weak}}$
and $W_x(x):=2mV(x)/\hbar^2$, so
$H^{\mathrm{free}}=(\hbar^2/2m)A_{0,x}$. Both $A_{0,x}$ and $W_x$
have inverse-square-length units; this energy division alone is not a
spatial nondimensionalization. Stationary items may abbreviate $W_x$ as $W$
(or its central radial profile as $w$), keeping physical $k$ and $r$.
The dimensionless operators instead satisfy
$$D_*H^{\mathrm{free}}D_*^*=E_*A_{0,*},\qquad D_*HD_*^*=E_*(A_{0,*}+M_{W_*}),\qquad W_*(y)=L_*^2W_x(L_*y).$$
Indeed testing the weak derivative definition after $x=L_*y$ gives
$\partial_y^\alpha D_*f=L_*^{|\alpha|}D_*(\partial_x^\alpha f)$ for
$|\alpha|\le2$; applying the inverse dilation gives the converse, so $D_*$
maps the physical Sobolev domain onto the dimensionless one. Multiplication
transforms by direct substitution, proving both operator identities on their
exact domains. The subscript $w$ in $\Delta_w$ above denotes weak derivatives,
not a coordinate or a unit convention.
With $M_V$ the maximal multiplication operator, $D(M_V)=\{f\in L^2:Vf\in L^2\}$ (bounded and everywhere defined in the compact-support class), the **assigned energy observables** of the model with declared
potential $V$ are the free operator $H^{\mathrm{free}}$ and the interacting
operator
$$H:=H^{\mathrm{free}}+M_{V},\qquad D(H):=D(H^{\mathrm{free}}).$$
The declared energy unit is the joule. For the compact-support class,
clause (c) of the cited theorem makes $H$ self-adjoint on $D(H)$ and bounded
below by $-\|V\|_{\infty}$; for the resolvent-tail class, self-adjointness of
$H$ on the same domain is proved on this page and is not presupposed here. The
model adopts $(H^{\mathrm{free}},\mathrm J)$ and $(H,\mathrm J)$ as assigned
sharp observables in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a), and
reads their flows by [[def-nrqm-autonomous-dynamics-framework-evolution]]
with $U_{\mathrm{free}}(t)=e^{-itH^{\mathrm{free}}/\hbar}$ and
$U(t)=e^{-itH/\hbar}$.

(a) **Position observable.** $Q_{j}$ is self-adjoint with domain $D(Q_{j})=\{\psi\in H:x_{j}\psi\in H\}$, its spectral PVM is given by $E_{Q_{j}}(B)\psi=\mathbf 1_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}\psi$, and
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}|\psi(x)|^{2}\,dx\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}).$$
The law is absolutely continuous with respect to one-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Its density is the $L^{1}(\mathbb R)$ equivalence class $f_{j}$ given for almost every $t$ by
$$f_{j}(t):=\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}|\psi(x_{\perp},t)|^{2}\,dx_{\perp};$$
this class is independent of the chosen representative of $\psi$ and is the $j$-th marginal density of $|\psi|^{2}$. The law is atomless: $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every $\lambda\in\mathbb R$. Moreover $\sigma(Q_{j})=\mathbb R$.

(c) **Momentum observable.** $P_{j}$ is self-adjoint with domain $D(P_{j})=\{\psi\in H:\xi_{j}\mathcal F_{2}\psi\in L^{2}\}$ and Fourier representation $\mathcal F_{2}(P_{j}\psi)(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\,\xi_{j}\,\mathcal F_{2}\psi(\xi)$; its spectral PVM is $E_{P_{j}}(B)=\mathcal F_{2}^{-1}M_{\mathbf 1_{m^{-1}(B)}}\mathcal F_{2}$ with $m(\xi)=2\pi\hbar\xi_{j}$, and
$$\mu^{P_{j}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{m^{-1}(B)}|\mathcal F_{2}\psi(\xi)|^{2}\,d\xi,\qquad m^{-1}(B)=\{\xi\in\mathbb R^{3}:2\pi\hbar\xi_{j}\in B\}.$$
The law is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure in the momentum variable $p$. Its density is the $L^{1}(\mathbb R)$ equivalence class $g_{j}$ given for almost every $p$ by
$$g_{j}(p)=\frac{1}{2\pi\hbar}\int_{\mathbb R^{2}}\bigl|\mathcal F_{2}\psi\bigl(\xi_{\perp},\tfrac{p}{2\pi\hbar}\bigr)\bigr|^{2}d\xi_{\perp}$$
where the class is independent of the chosen representative of $\mathcal F_{2}\psi$. The law is atomless; moreover $\sigma(P_{j})=\mathbb R$.

If the representative of $\psi$ changes on a Lebesgue-null subset of $\mathbb R^3$, Tonelli shows that the slice function changes only on a null subset of $\mathbb R$, so it defines a representative-independent $L^1(\mathbb R)$ class with integral $1$. For the atomless claim, Tonelli gives $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=\int_{\{\lambda\}}f_{j}(t)dt=0$ because $\{\lambda\}$ is countable hence Lebesgue-null [F6]. This proves clause (a). pair of alternative path conditions; and two unit vectors $e_{1},e_{2}\in K$,
the **marker states** correlated with the alternatives. The assignment of

data in the sense of P7; it is not computed from the framework, and no element
of this definition asserts that a particle described by the model "took" one
of the two alternatives. A declared marked model is **overlap-normalized**

$$V(B):=\frac{\sup_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)-\inf_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)}{\sup_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)+\inf_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)}\qquad\text{whenever }\sup_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)+\inf_{\varphi\in I}p(\varphi)(B)>0,$$

that the marker is measured or read out, that the alternatives are physically
realized, or that the loss of contrast described by $V$ is caused by any
particular process; the quantitative statement about $V$ is the content of a
separate theorem of this page.

Adopt the observable and probability postulate in the reading of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]], the kinematics
and massive-particle model postulate P5, and the internal-factor assignment of
the postulate P6, all read for the spin-$s$ model of
[[def-nrqm-kinematics-framework-massive-spin-s-model]] with mass parameter
$m>0$, spin label $s\in\{0,\tfrac12,1,\dots\}$ and $r=2s+1$
([[post-nrqm-framework-observable-and-probability]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-nonrelativistic-kinematics-and-massive-particle]],
[[post-nrqm-framework-identical-particles-and-spin]]), and assume the Axiom of
Countable Choice and the Axiom of Choice ([[def-countable-choice]],
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $H_{s}$ be the model's state space, $Q_{j},P_{k}$
its componentwise position and momentum operators, $U^{(s)}$ its momentum
transform, and let $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$ be the outcome law
of an assigned sharp observable $A$ in a unit vector $\psi$
([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (b)).
Then:

(a) for each $j$ the spectral projection-valued measure of $Q_{j}$ is
$$E_{Q_{j}}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}}\qquad(B\subseteq\mathbb R\ \text{Borel}),$$
the componentwise multiplication by the indicator, and
$$\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dx;$$
the law is atomless, $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ for every
$\lambda\in\mathbb R$, and $\sigma(Q_{j})=\mathbb R$;

(c) for each $k$ the spectral projection-valued measure of $P_{k}$ is
$$E_{P_{k}}(B)=U^{(s)-1}M_{\mathbf 1_{B}(p_{k})}U^{(s)},$$
and with $\psi_{p}:=U^{(s)}\psi$
$$\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi}(B)=\int_{\{p\in\mathbb R^{3}:\,p_{k}\in B\}}\|\psi_{p}(p)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}\,dp;$$
the law is atomless and $\sigma(P_{k})=\mathbb R$;

(e) **Scope.** The statement is conditional on P2, P5 and P6 and the cited
mathematics, and extends the position and momentum laws of the massive model to
the spin-$s$ state space. No joint law of a position and a momentum observable
is asserted, no dynamics is used or claimed, and the identification of the
operators with concrete laboratory apparatus is a tested identification under
the preparation and apparatus postulate, not a consequence of this theorem;
no empirical result is recorded. Exact values have probability zero although
both spectra equal $\mathbb R$. The real outcome spaces remain $\mathbb R$;
zero singleton mass means atomlessness and supplies no normalizable exact-value
eigenstate. Finite-resolution records use the displayed Borel bin probabilities.

[F1] **Outcome law.** For an assigned sharp observable $A$ with spectral PVM $E_{A}$ the law in a unit vector is $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{A}(B)\psi\|^{2}$, a probability measure on the Borel sets; the spectral support of $E_{A}$ is the spectrum $\sigma(A)$, and $\mu^{A}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$ unless $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue of $A$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clauses (b)-(d)). If $A$ has no eigenvalues its laws are atomless, with real outcome space $\mathbb R$ and no normalizable exact-value eigenstate; zero singleton mass does not exclude real point realizations (clause (c) of the same definition, [[def-projection-valued-measure]]).

[F5] **Measure toolkit.** For $\sigma$-finite measure spaces, integrals of nonnegative product-measurable functions may be iterated ([[thm-tonelli-theorem-for-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]); for nonnegative measurable $h$ the set function $A\mapsto\int_{A}h\,d\mu$ is a measure ([[thm-indefinite-integral-of-a-nonnegative-function-is-a-measure]]); finite measures on the $\sigma$-algebra generated by a $\pi$-system that agree on the $\pi$-system and have equal mass are equal ([[lem-finite-measure-uniqueness-on-a-pi-system]]); the Euclidean Borel $\sigma$-algebra of $\mathbb R^{3}$ is generated by the rectangles ([[thm-borel-products-of-euclidean-spaces-are-euclidean-borel]]). Under Countable Choice, every Borel measure finite on compact sets on a second-countable locally compact Hausdorff space is regular ([[cor-second-countable-lch-locally-finite-borel-measures-are-regular]]). The usual Euclidean $\mathbb R^3$ is such a space: rational-center, positive rational-radius balls form a countable base; the metric is Hausdorff; and closed bounded balls are compact by [[thm-heine-borel-rn]], so every point has a compact neighborhood. A coordinate hyperplane in $\mathbb R^{3}$ has Lebesgue measure zero: its indicator has iterated integral zero by [F5] because the inner integral over a singleton vanishes.

1.1 [Position spectral measure and law] [F2] gives $E_{Q_{j}}(B)=M_{\mathbf 1_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}}$, so for a unit $\psi$, $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{Q_{j}}(B)\psi\|^{2} =\int_{x_{j}^{-1}(B)}\|\psi(x)\|_{\mathbb C^{r}}^{2}dx$ by [F1] and the definition of the componentwise norm. The measure is the indefinite integral $A\mapsto\int_{A}\|\psi\|^{2}dx$ of a nonnegative integrable function [F5], hence atomless: for every $\lambda$ the set $x_{j}^{-1}(\{\lambda\})$ is a coordinate hyperplane, whose indicator has iterated integral zero by [F5], so $\mu^{Q_{j}}_{\psi}(\{\lambda\})=0$. Finally the essential range of $x_{j}$ is $\mathbb R$ because every interval slab $x_{j}^{-1}((\lambda-\varepsilon,\lambda+\varepsilon))$ has positive Lebesgue measure, so [F4] gives $\sigma(Q_{j})=\mathbb R$. This proves (a). [F1, F2, F4, F5, algebra]

2.2 [Momentum spectral measure and law] By [F3] and [F4], $U^{(s)}$ is unitary, $D(M_{p_{k}})=U^{(s)}D(P_{k})$ and $M_{p_{k}}=U^{(s)}P_{k}U^{(s)-1}$; the multiplication operator $M_{p_{k}}$ on $L^{2}(dp;\mathbb C^{r})$ is self-adjoint with spectral PVM $M_{\mathbf 1_{\{p_{k}\in B\}}}$ [F4], so transporting through the unitary $U^{(s)}$ and using uniqueness of the spectral PVM [F4] gives $E_{P_{k}}(B)=U^{(s)-1}M_{\mathbf 1_{\{p_{k}\in B\}}}U^{(s)}$. For a unit $\psi$, $\mu^{P_{k}}_{\psi}(B)=\|E_{P_{k}}(B)\psi\|^{2} =\|M_{\mathbf 1_{\{p_{k}\in B\}}}U^{(s)}\psi\|^{2} =\int_{\{p_{k}\in B\}}\|\psi_{p}(p)\|^{2}dp$ [F3]. The law is the indefinite integral of the integrable function $\|\psi_{p}\|^{2}$ over a slice condition, hence atomless by the hyperplane argument of step 1.1; and the essential range of $p_{k}$ is $\mathbb R$, so $\sigma(P_{k})=\mathbb R$ [F4]. This proves (c). [step 1.1, F3, F4, algebra]

- **Relation to the spinless laws.** For $s=0$ one has $r=1$ and the statement
  reduces to the position and momentum outcome laws of the spinless massive
  model already established on the observables page; the present theorem
  supplies the component-valued case and the invariance of the spatial laws
  under the internal factor.
- **Nondegenerate continuum.** Both spectra equal $\mathbb R$ and both laws are
  atomless: the model admits no normalizable position or momentum eigenvector,
  and no exact value is an outcome with positive probability. Finite-resolution
  readings are the Borel bin probabilities displayed above.

=\{f\in H_{\mathrm{lin}}:|\xi|^{2}\mathcal F_{2}f\in H_{\mathrm{lin}}\}$,
where $\mathcal F_{2}$ is the unitary Plancherel transform of that theorem
([[thm-nrqm-composites-real-multipliers-and-free-bounded-potential-operators]]
clauses (a)-(c)). The declared energy unit is the joule. By
[[lem-nrqm-potentials-free-operator-differential-identification]] the domain
$D(H_{V})$ is the Sobolev space $W^{2,2}(\mathbb R;\mathbb C)$ and
$$H_{V}f=-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\,D^{2}f+Vf\qquad(f\in D(H_{V})),$$
$D^{2}$ the second weak derivative, so the model's time-independent equation
inside any open interval on which $V$ is (say) constant is the ordinary
differential equation $-\frac{\hbar^{2}}{2m}\psi''+V\psi=E\psi$. The model
adopts $(H_{V},\mathrm J)$ as its assigned energy observable in the sense of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (a); its
self-adjointness is established by the line-model energy theorem of this page
and is not presupposed here. A declared potential is **compactly supported** when $V$
vanishes almost everywhere outside some bounded interval.

the model with potential $V$ and energy $E\in\mathbb R$ is a nonzero class
$\psi\in D(H_{V})$ with $H_{V}\psi=E\psi$; the pair $(\psi,E)$ is an
**eigenpair** of the model. A **bound state** of the model is a stationary
solution with energy $E<0$ whose representative is normalized, $\|\psi\|=1$;
its eigenvalue $E$ is its **signed binding energy**, read in joules, and its
positive binding-energy magnitude is $-E$. The value $0$ is the reference
energy in this negative-eigenvalue definition of a bound state. For a general
bounded measurable $V$, this convention makes no assertion about the location
of any spectral threshold. The model reads the
energy outcome law of the pure preparation of a unit eigenstate $\psi$ with
eigenvalue $E$ through clause (a) of
[[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] as the point
mass $\delta_{E}$ at $E$, so that outcome in $\{E\}$ has probability one; and
the position density of the preparation is $|\psi|^{2}$ by clause (b). These
readings are declarations of the model under P2 and construct no sample,
detector or measured value.

composite of the two internal factors $V\widehat\otimes V$, define the total
spin component for each $i\in\{x,y,z\}$ by
$$S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}:=S_i\otimes I_V+I_V\otimes S_i.$$

$S_{n}\otimes I_V$ or $I_V\otimes S_n$, read as a bounded assigned sharp
observable of its factor with unit $\mathrm{J\,s}$
([[def-nrqm-angular-momentum-framework-angular-momentum-observables]] clause
(c), [[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]]). Put
$$\Psi:=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\bigl(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})-\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+})\bigr),\qquad \rho:=T_{\Psi,\Psi}\in D(V\widehat\otimes V),$$

**(a) Singlet data.** $\Psi$ is a unit vector; $S^{\mathrm{tot}}_{i}\Psi=0$ for
all $i$; $\rho_{A}=\rho_{B}=\tfrac12 I$; and the Schmidt expansion of $\Psi$
is $\Psi=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\bigl(\kappa(e_{+}\otimes e_{-})-\kappa(e_{-}\otimes e_{+})\bigr)$

$$G_{a,b}(C):=\sum_{(\varepsilon,\delta)\in C}P_{a,\varepsilon}\otimes P_{b,\delta}\qquad(C\subseteq\{-1,+1\}^{2}).$$

[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]], its
coordinate representatives $f(k)$ have units $\mathrm m^{3/2}$. Put
$\varepsilon(k)=\hbar c|k|$, and let
$\rho_{f}$ be the one-photon preparation of the ray of $\iota_{1}(f)$. Then:

(d) *no sharp frequency, energy or momentum*: for every unit vector
$f\in D(\varepsilon_{\mathfrak h})$, the variances of the frequency and energy
laws of (b) are strictly positive, and for every unit vector in
$D(M_{\hbar k_j}^{\mathfrak h})$ the momentum-component variance of (c) is
strictly positive; consequently the mode assignment "photon energy $E=\hbar\omega$,
$\omega=c|k|$" is a spectral assignment of the model and never an exact value
of a normalisable one-photon state;

[F7] **Means and variances for pure states.** For a self-adjoint $A$ and a unit $u\in D(A)$ the mean of the outcome law in the pure state $T_{u,u}$ is $\langle Au,u\rangle$; the variance is $\|Au\|^{2}-\langle Au,u\rangle^{2}$ when $u\in D(A)$ ([[def-nrqm-observables-framework-observable-and-outcome-law]] clause (e)).

**The Gaussian packet.** [[ex-nrqm-kinematics-gaussian-position-momentum-packet]]
computes, in the spin-zero massive model, the normalized Gaussian
$\psi_{\sigma}(x)=(\pi\sigma^{2})^{-3/4}e^{-|x|^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})}$, shows
that its momentum representative is again a normalized Gaussian with width
$\sigma_{p}=\hbar/\sigma$, and evaluates the position and momentum outcome
densities of the model together with their variances $\sigma^{2}/2$ and
$\hbar^{2}/(2\sigma^{2})$ and the product $\hbar/2$. This verifies the model's
sharp laws of [[pthm-nrqm-kinematics-spin-s-outcome-laws]] on a family of
Schwartz preparations; it computes no dynamics, no measurement and no general
uncertainty statement.

**The plane wave as a generalized functional.** [[ex-nrqm-kinematics-plane-wave-generalized-eigenfunction]]
defines the conjugate-linear functional $u_{k}(\varphi)=\int e^{ik\cdot
x}\overline{\varphi}$ on Schwartz classes, proves the eigenrelation
$u_{k}(P_{j}\varphi)=\hbar k_{j}u_{k}(\varphi)$, and proves that no $L^{2}$
class represents $u_{k}$. This is the precise sense in which the plane wave is
a generalized momentum eigenfunction: it diagonalizes the momentum action on
the test space while carrying no state or probability density. The framework's
state assignment excludes it as a preparation, in agreement with the model's
atomless sharp laws.

**What the page proves conditionally.**
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-fixed-mode-polarization-model]] and
[[def-nrqm-photons-framework-radiation-sector-and-quantum-assignments]] fix the
model vocabulary, units and domains.
[[pthm-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-polarization-outcome-law]] proves the Born
outcome law $\cos^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$, $\sin^{2}(\theta-\varphi)$ of the
declared ideal analyser, its affinity over mixtures, its phase invariance and
the conditional update of a repeated ideal analyser.
[[pthm-nrqm-photons-one-photon-number-energy-and-momentum-laws]] proves that a
normalisable one-photon preparation has the sharp number readout one, the
frequency and energy laws given by the push-forwards of $\|f(k)\|^{2}\,d^{3}k$
under $c|k|$ and $\hbar c|k|$ (a unit packet coordinate $f(k)$ has units
$\mathrm m^{3/2}$ under $d^{3}k$), their means under the first-moment condition, and
the corresponding momentum-component laws and means under absolute
first-moment integrability. Frequency, energy and momentum variances are
strictly positive and finite on the corresponding multiplier domains; the
singleton probabilities vanish for every normalisable unit vector without a
moment-domain hypothesis.
[[pthm-nrqm-photons-fixed-mode-number-and-energy-statistics]] proves the sharp
count of the $n$-quanta mode state, the Poisson count law and moments of the
mode-coherent preparation, the energy means and variances of those
preparations, and that $e^{-\beta H_f}$ is not trace class for the full
continuum sector when $\beta>0$ has unit $\mathrm J^{-1}$. Thus its
trace-normalized full-sector Gibbs density is unavailable; other preparations
are outside the theorem. All these are conditional consequences of P1, P2 and
the adopted radiation model; their units are recorded in
[[def-nrqm-framework-quantities-and-units]] and in the assigned observables
of the model.

[[ex-nrqm-potentials-rectangular-barrier-tunnelling-and-thick-limit]] treats
the rectangular barrier of [[pthm-nrqm-potentials-barrier-flux-and-transmission]]

theorem's error bound $201/125000=0.001608$; the computation is a finite check
of the model formulas, including the positivity of transmission through a
classically forbidden barrier.
[[ex-nrqm-potentials-finite-well-exact-root-and-count]] exhibits a declared
well depth at which the unique bound state is exactly solvable (even state,
$k=\kappa=\pi/(4a)$, binding energy $E=-U/2=-\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}/(32ma^{2})$),
verifies the even root condition with the special value $\tan(\pi/4)=1$, and
verifies the count and branch criterion at declared depths: exactly three
bound states with types even, odd, even when $2aK/\pi=5/2$, exactly one when
$2aK/\pi=1$, exactly two when $2aK/\pi=2$, and at least one for every
$a,U>0$.

box eigenpairs $\mathcal E_{n}=\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}n^{2}/(2mL^{2})$ with sine

$\mathcal E_{n}+c$ of a constant potential with the min-max bound attained,
and the positive gaps $\hbar^{2}\pi^{2}(2n+1)/(2mL^{2})$.
